Minimal directional easing signal (Maybe True, 50.005) from one small uncontrolled Japanese PD series testing liquid lemon juice as a gastric acidifier alongside levodopa in hypochlorhydric patients, heavily tempered by qualitative abstract reporting, null overall elderly ascorbic-acid PK, and carbidopa-stability limits. Capped strictly at minimal_signal (50.005) pending controlled PD trials.

Minimal directional easing signal (Maybe True, 50.005) supported by three independent neurogenic dysphagia clinical trials testing fresh lemon juice or equivalent citric acid sour boluses, tempered by non-PD cohorts, randomized-sequence carryover nulls, and distal esophageal slowing. In Gunes 2026 (PMID:42642850, PMC13507510, NCT07400822; parallel RCT in 95 acute ischemic stroke patients with mild-moderate dysphagia, excluding severe dysphagia/drooling), 4 mL freshly squeezed room-temperature lemon juice (pH 2.8) given 3x/day before meals for 7 days significantly improved Gugging Swallowing Screen (GUSS) total scores versus 4 mL water on Day 7 (Z=-3.692, p<0.001, r=0.38, MD +2.50 pts) and Day 30 (Z=-5.228, p<0.001, r=0.54, MD +3.54 pts; GUSS direct p<0.001, r=0.56), while NIHSS stroke severity did not differ (p>0.05). In Logemann 1995 (PMID:7674647; VFSS crossover in 27 neurogenic dysphagia patients: 19 stroke + 8 other neurogenic), a 50% lemon juice / 50% barium sour bolus improved oral swallow onset in both groups, shortened pharyngeal delay in stroke, and reduced aspiration in non-stroke neurogenic dysphagia. In Pelletier & Lawless 2003 (PMID:14571326; FEES in 11 neurogenic dysphagia residents), 2.7% citric acid (bridged to fresh lemon juice 1.44 g/oz via Penniston 2008 PMC2637791) reduced aspiration/penetration vs water and increased spontaneous dry swallows. CRITICAL OPPOSING/SAFETY CAVEATS: Cola 2012 (PMID:23139681, PMC3493000; n=60 stroke) and Gatto 2021 (PMID:33549862; n=52) found lemon-flavored sour-cold paste failed to differ significantly across stimuli under randomized presentation order due to carryover; Alves 2013 (PMID:22642501; n=36 chronic stroke + 30 controls) showed low-pH sour liquid (pH 3.0) PROLONGED distal esophageal transit and clearance; Gunes 2026 lacked VFSS/FEES confirmation and noted severe-dysphagia patients expelled lemon juice as drooling; and ZERO trials have tested raw lemon juice in diagnosed Parkinson's disease dysphagia. Thin acidic liquids carry aspiration/coughing and dental-erosion risks and require supervised small-volume protocols.

Remains Unknown (Researched, 50) — CRITICAL CYP3A4 CONTRAST AGAINST GRAPEFRUIT (R4 0451 / 0466): Unlike grapefruit juice, a direct human randomized crossover trial comparing 250 mL grapefruit juice vs 250 mL quarter-strength lime juice (Citrus aurantifolia, containing 100 uM bergamottin -- 4x higher than grapefruit's 25 uM!) with felodipine proved that quarter-strength lime juice DID NOT SIGNIFICANTLY ALTER MEAN FELODIPINE AUC OR CMAX vs water (Bailey 2003 PMID:12811362; grapefruit nearly doubled AUC 55 vs 29 nmol*h/L, p<0.05; lime juice mean null, though 2 individual outliers exceeded 2-fold elevation). Chen 2018 (PMC9326888, 46-RCT review) similarly confirms lime juice has not precipitated clinically severe CYP3A4 toxicity in RCTs, while animal carbamazepine interaction data (Karmakar 2015 PMC9351769) are preclinical only. Human lime peel/rind trials show NO blood pressure lowering vs placebo (Hashemipour 2016 PMC5307599, n=59 triple-masked RCT; Ammatalli 2024 PMC11305151, n=60 crossover; note Bukhari 2022 PMID:35646151 was RETRACTED and excluded). Zero clinical studies show cooked lime worsens or eases daytime sleepiness severity in PD, though clinicians should remain cautious with large volumes of full-strength lime juice alongside narrow-therapeutic CYP3A4 drugs given Bailey 2003's individual outliers.

Remains Unknown (Researched, 50) — CRITICAL CYP3A4 CONTRAST AGAINST GRAPEFRUIT (R4 0451 / 0466): Unlike grapefruit juice, a direct human randomized crossover trial comparing 250 mL grapefruit juice vs 250 mL quarter-strength lime juice (Citrus aurantifolia, containing 100 uM bergamottin -- 4x higher than grapefruit's 25 uM!) with felodipine proved that quarter-strength lime juice DID NOT SIGNIFICANTLY ALTER MEAN FELODIPINE AUC OR CMAX vs water (Bailey 2003 PMID:12811362; grapefruit nearly doubled AUC 55 vs 29 nmol*h/L, p<0.05; lime juice mean null, though 2 individual outliers exceeded 2-fold elevation). Maybe False (minimal_signal toward easing, 50.005): Zero human clinical evidence suggests macadamia nuts worsen depressive symptoms; on the contrary, the sole human macadamia-nut RCT assessing a validated depression instrument (Somerset 2011, PMID:21575998, Clin Nutr, n=64 overweight adults BMI >27, pre-existing major depression excluded) randomized participants for 10 weeks to usual diet vs an isocaloric MUFA-enriched diet replacing saturated fat by adding macadamia nuts (both arms given identical physical-activity advice and consultations) and reported that Beck Depression Inventory-II (BDI-II) scores decreased in the macadamia-MUFA group while increasing in the control group (univariate ANOVA adjusted R2=0.257, p=0.01). Major limitations constrain certainty strictly to minimal_signal: high depression-linked attrition before week 10 (baseline BDI-II >=10 strongly predicted dropout, p<0.001; R=-0.38 with retention, p<0.05), bundled SFA-to-MUFA dietary replacement, unspecified raw vs roasted nut grade, non-PD sample, and paywalled full text (exact completer counts and arm BDI-II means not printed in PubMed abstract). All other human macadamia-nut RCTs (Curb 2000, Garg 2003, Griel 2008, Jones 2023) measured only cardiometabolic lipids; RRIPP-3 (Marriott 2021, PMC8228047) tested encapsulated macadamia OIL as krill-oil comparator (POMS depressed p=0.2103, no oil-free arm); and canine macadamia toxicosis "CNS depression" (Hansen 2000, PMID:10670081) is acute veterinary lethargy in dogs that does NOT transfer to human depression. Minimal indirect clinical signal that raw fresh whole mango eases chronic functional constipation in non-PD adults, opposing the frozen 'worsens' claim as Maybe False (50.005). Anchored on Venancio et al. 2018 (PMID:29733520, Mol Nutr Food Res, n=36 adults with chronic functional constipation randomized for 4 weeks to 300 g/day fresh Mangifera indica fruit vs equivalent isolated fiber [~5 g/day psyllium]): fresh mango significantly improved constipation status (stool frequency, consistency, and shape) beyond equivalent fiber, while elevating plasma gastrin and fecal valeric acid and lowering plasma endotoxin and IL-6—cited within the Grade B fruit-based laxative category of Rao & Brenner 2021 (PMC8191753, Am J Gastroenterol). Crucially, adversarial and matrix limitations strictly constrain confidence to minimal_signal (50.005): (1) a 12-week crossover RCT in n=27 non-constipated overweight/obese young adults (Kim/Rosas cohort, PMID:37051355, PMC10084975; 100 kcal/d [~165 g, 2.6 g fiber] fresh mango vs low-fat cookies) found a modest within-arm increase in stool volume (1.10->1.23 cups/d, p<0.05) but COMPLETELY NULL differences within or between arms for bowel movement frequency, stool consistency, straining, pain, or constipation rating (baseline frequency 1.69/day = floor effect, zero worsening); (2) Venancio 2018 was a small (n=36), open-label, industry-supported single-center pilot lacking independent replication (hence excluded from BDA 2025 guidelines which required >=2 chronic constipation RCTs); (3) Kim 2020 (PMID:32109839, n=10 single-arm IBD pilot, 200-400 g/d mango pulp) assessed colitis activity rather than constipation; and (4) ZERO clinical trials exist in Parkinson's disease constipation. Cultural/community context aligns qualitatively without adding efficacy weight (Ayurvedic Amra ripe pulp mild laxative heritage, PMC5804368; Parkinson's UK forum threads t/14613 and t/1164 mentioning mango smoothies/soluble fiber alongside co-interventions). Safety & matrix note: fresh mango pulp carries rare IgE/exercise-induced anaphylaxis risk (Dore 2026 PMC13251668) and peel urushiol contact allergy; proprietary mango LEAF extracts (Zynamite, Zynamite S, Stadice) and unrelated Irvingia gabonensis ('African bush mango') are strictly excluded.

Remains Unknown (Researched): Although Nigella sativa is widely marketed as anxiolytic and shows anxiolytic-like EPM effects in several oral rodent models (including 6-OHDA PD rats given 50 mg/kg oral thymoquinone; Pala 2024, PMID:38660812), full-text audit of BOTH direct human anxiety double-blind RCTs shows NULL between-group anxiety effects: (1) Rafiee Zadeh 2022 (PMID:35548175, PMC9081508; n=52 male MDD on sertraline + 1,000 mg/d oral N. sativa oil x 10 wk) reported Table 2 DASS-21 Anxiety post-treatment 21.7 +/- 3 vs 21.7 +/- 3 (p=0.545; change -1.96 vs -1.32, p=0.572) and DASS-21 Stress p=0.207/0.167 (null between groups); (2) Bin Sayeed 2014 (PMID:24412554; n=48 healthy adolescent males, 500 mg/d ground seed x 4 wk) found NO significant between-group difference on STAI State or Trait anxiety. Mohan 2023 (PMC10149792; n=72 non-restorative sleep, industry-funded 200 mg/d TQ-rich oil BCO-5) significantly lowered Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-14, p<0.001) and salivary cortisol, but PSS-14 measures perceived stress rather than a validated clinical anxiety scale and used proprietary 5%-TQ oil (whereas roasting/toasting degrades TQ; Veeriah 2023). Moreover, rodent oral N. sativa oil EPM anxiety was inconsistent/absent in Cheema 2018 (PMID:27868798). Two null direct human anxiety RCTs plus roasting TQ loss leave toasted nigella seed on PD anxiety unresolved. Safety caveats: Nigella sativa (black seed / black cumin) is botanically distinct from Cuminum cyminum (cumin); high-temperature roasting significantly degrades thymoquinone (Veeriah 2023); oral supplementation lowers seated systolic BP modestly (~3 mmHg in meta-analyses, though null in elderly HTN RCT Rizka 2017 with zero orthostatic hypotension), warranting monitoring in PD patients with orthostatic hypotension, antihypertensives, or antidiabetic therapy; high-dose thymoquinone caused rodent rotarod impairment (Hosseinzadeh 2016) and CYP/drug-interaction caution applies.

Preclinical oral rodent analgesia results are inconsistent and chemically remote from culinary grated nutmeg: while continuous oral steam-distilled nutmeg essential oil (10-20 mg/kg/d x 3 wk) reduced CFA inflammatory paw swelling, mechanical allodynia, heat hyperalgesia, COX-2, and Substance P in rats (Zhang 2016, PMID:27121041, PMC4848392—with authors explicitly warning safrole/myristicin/elemicin toxicity requires human safety evaluation) and chloroform extract reduced writhing (Olajide 1999, PMID:10404545), petroleum-ether extract was NULL for analgesia in Grover 2002 (PMID:12616960) and oral seed alkaloids (Hayfaa 2013, PMID:23946667) reduced writhing ONLY in female mice while remaining NULL in male mice and NULL at 0.5 g/kg. Minimal indirect clinical and prospective signal that cold-pressed/extra-virgin olive oil (EVOO) reduces depressive symptom severity, supporting the reducing hypothesis as Maybe True (50.005). In a 52-day double-blind RCT in 73 patients with major depressive disorder (Foshati 2022, PMID:34358723), 25 mL/day EVOO reduced HAMD-7 (p = 0.001) and BDI-II (p = 0.021) scores more than sunflower oil—driven by severe depression (p = 0.017/0.008; null in mild-to-moderate), without cortisol or BDNF change and subject to a published methodological letter (Flynn 2022, PMID:35276417). Prospective EPIC-Greece data (Kyrozis 2009, PMID:18952225, n = 610 elders) also linked olive oil inversely to high Geriatric Depression Scale scores 6-13 years later, and exploratory DieTBra within-arm (-55.2%, Canheta 2021, tempered by Eckert 2020 critique) and TANDIM post-hoc (Staudacher 2025, n = 48, p = 0.03) analyses aligned directionally. Substantial contrary/null trials cap certainty at minimal_signal: whole-diet PREDIMED MD+EVOO did not reduce incident depression (Sánchez-Villegas 2013, PMC3848350, n = 3,923), PREDIDEP MD+EVOO was null on primary recurrence (Cabrera-Suárez 2024, PMID:37990906, n = 196; secondary BDI improved), Religa 2026 (PMC13713344, n = 115) found null HADS depression (adj p = 0.422), and omega-3 trials using olive oil capsules as placebo (Gertsik 2012, Silvers 2005, Meyer 2013, Sousa 2023) lacked oil-free arms. No isolated cold-pressed olive oil depression trial exists in Parkinson's disease.

Minimal prospective human signal that common/refined olive oil is associated with worse 2-year executive function trajectory, opposing the claim that refined olive oil reduces executive function impairment (Maybe False, 50.005). In the 2-year prospective PREDIMED-Plus cohort (Ni 2026, PMID:41578342, PMC12910899, n = 656 overweight/metabolic-syndrome older adults), higher Common Olive Oil intake (COO: refined olive oil plus olive-pomace oil) was significantly associated with greater decline on the 4-test Executive Function composite (Verbal Fluency Animals/Letter-P, TMT-B, Digit Span Backward) in the fully adjusted model: beta = -0.047 z-score per 10 g/day (95% CI -0.083 to -0.011, p = 0.010) and top vs bottom tertile beta = -0.153 (95% CI -0.270 to -0.035, p-trend = 0.001)—persisting after sensitivity adjustment for other oils and directly contrasting with Virgin olive oil (+0.036 per 10 g/d, p = 0.002; T3 +0.156, p-trend = 0.003) in the same cohort. This differs sharply from Round 1 claim 0969 (refined olive oil & attention -> open), where COO attention was null (p = 0.771). In RCTs specifically assigning refined olive oil (ROO), Kaddoumi 2022 (PMC9736478, n = 25 MCI) did not measure executive function, lacked an oil-free control, and found ROO failed to improve BBB integrity or functional connectivity unlike EVOO; Patan 2021 (PMC8408864, n = 310) showed EPA outperformed 3 g/d ROO placebo on global speed/accuracy; and Yuuki 2026 (PMID:41443401, n = 36) showed MCT outperformed olive oil on inhibitory control and working memory. Strictly separated from high-phenolic EVOO trials (MICOIL Tsolaki 2020, PREDIMED-NAVARRA, Kanaan 2026 SR; MIND Barnes 2023 null p = 0.23). Observational design, pooling of refined and pomace oil, baseline smoking/education differences in T3 COO, and non-PD sample cap the opposing lean at minimal_signal.

Inconclusive and conflicting oral human evidence leaves extra-virgin olive oil (EVOO) and Parkinson's pain severity open (Unknown, 50). Full-text audit reveals that the two largest randomized controlled oral EVOO trials failed to show isolated EVOO pain relief: 1) FIBROKIT (Durán González 2026, PMC13301056, n = 250 women [206 fibromyalgia], 190 completed, 6-month double-blind EVOO vs ROO) explicitly reported NO differences across timepoints in any clinical outcome (FIQR, SF-36), failing to replicate the tiny 3-week pilot Rus 2017 (PMID:27443526, n = 23 women, FIQ/MCS-12); 2) DieTBra (Mendonça 2021, PMC8582684, n = 149 severe obesity, 12 weeks) found EVOO alone (52 mL/d) was completely NULL on every pain measure (Table 2: p = 0.132 to 0.564), with authors explicitly concluding 'EVOO alone was not effective in reducing pain in our study'—and although EVOO + DieTBra reduced severe pain prevalence vs DieTBra alone (-22.7% vs -9.8%, p = 0.003), DieTBra alone beat EVOO + DieTBra on wrist/hand (p = 0.014), upper back (p = 0.002), and knee pain (p = 0.016). An open-label trigeminal neuralgia pilot (Moreno 2024, PMID:38306883, n = 42 completed, 60 mL/d EVOO vs usual diet) showed within-arm Penn Facial Pain drops but no significant between-group pain-severity separation (orofacial interference trend p = 0.05). In RA, Berbert 2005 (PMID:15723739, n = 43) found no joint-pain difference between fish oil + olive oil and fish oil alone; Krenek 2025 (PMC12030687, n = 40) had null pooled SF-36 pain (p = 0.340). Preclinical mouse writhing analgesia used EVOO acetonitrile extract/oleocanthal (Chiang 2020, PMID:33008039), and topical massage/phonophoresis RCTs (Hekmatpou 2020, Nasiri 2022, Nakhostin-Roohi 2016) are non-oral. Minimal preclinical signal that oral whole onion (Allium cepa) bulb reduces anxiety-like behavior, supporting the reducing hypothesis as Maybe True (50.005). In a controlled male mouse immobilization-stress experiment (Samad & Saleem 2018, PMID:29178012), 14 days of oral whole A. cepa bulb powder (200 mg/kg/day in water) significantly attenuated stress-induced anxiety-like behavior on both the Elevated Plus Maze (EPM) and Light-Dark Activity (LDA) tests alongside brain antioxidant enzyme restoration. In humans, no randomized controlled trial has tested culinary raw onion on a validated clinical anxiety scale: full-text audit of an 8-week onion peel extract DB-RCT in 80 stressed adults (Cho 2024, PMC10861340, 1,000 mg/d OPE) shows total Perceived Stress Scale was NULL (Table 4: p = 0.164), and the single item 'felt nervous and stressed' (p = 0.021) reflected severe baseline imbalance (2.84 vs 2.27) with identical Week-8 scores (1.78 vs 1.73). An open-label T2DM trial of 500 mg/day isolated pharmaceutical quercetin capsules (Mantadaki 2024, PMC11205103, n = 88) reported lower SAST-10 anxiety (p < 0.001) but is strictly separated as an unblinded, >10x-dietary pharmaceutical isolate (exposure_fit = remote). Absence of human culinary-onion anxiety RCTs and non-PD rodent transfer cap the claim at minimal_signal.

Minimal indirect human clinical signal that quercetin-rich onion reduces apathy severity, opposing the worsening hypothesis as Maybe False (50.005). Full-text table audit of a 24-week double-blind, placebo-controlled parallel RCT in 70 healthy older Japanese adults (61 per-protocol; Nishihira 2021, PMID:34616111, PMC8482389, UMIN000036276—correcting prompt PMID typo 33781028) shows that 11 g/day air-dried quercetin-rich 'Sarasara Gold' onion powder (equivalent to ~120 g raw onion, 50 mg/d quercetin aglycone eq, consumed without cooking restriction) significantly reduced validated Apathy Scale scores compared with quercetin-free white onion powder placebo (Table 5: -2.6 +/- 3.8 vs -0.1 +/- 3.0, between-group p = 0.021). Exploratory support comes from Hayashi 2023 (PMC10391933, n = 19 MCI/AD DB-RCT), where quercetin-rich onion powder increased sentence adjectives/adverbs as a linguistic motivation proxy (p = 0.043) while MMSE total (p = 0.773), NPI, and rCBF were null. Key caveats cap certainty at minimal_signal: Apathy Scale was a secondary endpoint in healthy non-PD elders, baseline apathy was non-significantly higher in the active arm (6.4 +/- 4.8 vs 4.8 +/- 4.1, p = 0.217), the medication-free subclass attenuated to a non-significant trend (p = 0.099, n = 38), and the comparator was quercetin-free white onion powder (isolating quercetin-rich cultivars rather than raw onion vs an onion-free diet).

No human clinical trial demonstrates an attention benefit from cooked onion in Parkinson's disease or older adults (Unknown, 50). Similarly, Hayashi 2023 (PMC10391933, n = 19 MCI/AD DB-RCT) was completely NULL on MMSE total (p = 0.773) and all MMSE attention items, and Nakagawa 2016 (PMID:27145228, early AD) measured HDS-R memory recall rather than attention.

Short 5-day crossover duration, concentrated onion-extract tablets vs whole roasted onion, non-PD sample without diagnosed insomnia, paywalled full-text numeric tables, and lack of independent replication cap certainty at minimal_signal.

Topical onion-extract scar gels are non-oral and excluded. Remains Unknown (Researched, 50): No controlled human trial tests oral raw sweet orange on anxiety severity in PD or clinical anxiety cohorts. Prospective flavonoid cohorts (Gao 2012 PMID:22491871; Zhang 2022 PMID:35082171) evaluated PD incidence and all-cause mortality rather than apathy severity (with berries/anthocyanins rather than oranges driving inverse associations), isolated citrus limonin rodent data (Gao 2023 PMID:37536186) and sweet-orange essential-oil cell assays (Pandur 2025 PMC12801818) do not establish an oral raw-fruit symptom effect, and sweet orange is strictly distinguished from bitter/Seville orange (Citrus aurantium) and Kampo dried peel formulas.

In Alharbi 2016 (PMID:26280945, PMC5009163; n=22 completed healthy middle-aged men, DB-PC crossover of 240 mL 100% orange juice with 5.5 g whole-orange pomace fiber delivering 272 mg flavonoids), Continuous Performance Task (CPT) sustained-attention accuracy improved vs placebo (Drink x Time F[1,21]=3.96, p=0.05; 6 h commission errors -1.6 vs +0.6 placebo, t=2.02, p<0.05; 2 h NS; DSST and Serial Sevens NS). In Lamport 2016 (PMID:28091350; n=24 young adults crossover, 500 mL 70.5 mg flavanone citrus juice vs energy/vitamin-C-matched control), Digit Symbol Substitution Test (DSST) processing/attention speed improved at 2 h alongside increased right frontal gyrus CBF (n=16 ASL-fMRI), while other behavioral tests were null. Kean 2015 (PMID:25733635; n=37 older adults, 8-wk DB-PC crossover of 500 mL/d 305 mg vs 37 mg flavanone orange juice) improved global cognition (p<0.05). Opposing/tempering evidence: Cheng 2022 meta-analysis (PMID:35333451, PMC9787524; 80 RCTs) found the small citrus subgroup (k=3) had a positive Hedges g that did NOT reach pooled subgroup significance; Pinto 2023 (PMID:37902089) found 1.5 g orange pulp alone lacked acute cognitive gains seen with blackcurrant+orange pulp; and Giovannini 2026 (PMID:40694049) bundled hesperidin with diosmin and proanthocyanidins. Zero trials test peeled raw sweet orange in diagnosed PD attention impairment.

In Alharbi 2016 (PMID:26280945, PMC5009163; n=22 healthy middle-aged men, DB-PC crossover of 240 mL whole-pomace flavonoid-rich orange juice), an unadjusted exploratory analysis of the single PANAS mood adjective 'alertness' showed a borderline omnibus drink effect (F[1,21]=4.1, p=0.05; -0.5% vs -6.4% decline over 6 h), BUT individual 2-h and 6-h pairwise contrasts did NOT reach significance, global PANAS Positive/Negative Affect were null, Kean 2015 (PMID:25733635, n=37 older adults, 8 wk) found no mood effect, and no validated sleepiness (ESS) or clinical fatigue (FSS/MFI) instrument was administered. Minimal indirect human clinical signal that whole oyster mushroom (Pleurotus ostreatus) reduces anxiety severity, opposing the worsening hypothesis as Maybe False (50.005). In the 12-week OYSCOG randomized placebo-controlled trial in 80 healthy older adults aged 60-80 years (Cha 2026, PMID:42299921, NCT06846827), four weekly portions of dried whole P. ostreatus improved DASS-21 anxiety within the mushroom group while anxiety rose in the placebo group, resulting in significantly lower DASS-21 anxiety for oyster mushroom vs placebo at 12 weeks alongside reduced ex vivo microglial COX-2 and NOX-2. This signal is balanced against a null 8-week controlled feeding RCT in 60 middle-aged/older adults (Uffelman 2024, PMC11311880, NCT04259229) combining white button (4 d/wk) and oyster mushrooms (3 d/wk) inside a Mediterranean diet, which found no difference on GAD-7 (p = 0.74) or POMS Tension-Anxiety (p = 0.543). Strictly separated from Lion's Mane (Hericium erinaceus) and marine oysters (Crassostrea). Non-PD healthy older adults, dried/prepared whole mushroom vs specifically roasted preparation, paywalled OYSCOG numeric tables, and the competing mixed-species null trial cap certainty at minimal_signal.

Minimal directional easing signal opposing the frozen 'worsens' claim (Maybe False, 50.005) from a double-blind placebo-controlled human RCT of a concentrated organic ripe Carica papaya fruit pulp preparation (Caricol), aligned with strong Southeast Asian ethnobotanical consensus and zero clinical evidence of constipation worsening. In Muss 2013 (PMID:23524622; Neuro Endocrinol Lett 2013; 139 enrolled / 126 completed per clinical reporting), adults with chronic gastrointestinal dysfunction consumed 20 mL/day Caricol vs placebo for 40 days: among early returnees evaluated within 2 days of completion, Caricol produced statistically significant improvements in primary endpoints 'constipation' and 'bloating' versus placebo, whereas benefits dissipated after an 8.6 +/- 5.95-day washout ('late returnees'), demonstrating reversible active efficacy (heartburn was non-significant, n=13, p=0.114). Contextual records align directionally without supplying independent causal proof: Leao 2011 (PMID:21537543; n=12 uncontrolled Chagas megacolon cohort combining pelvic physiotherapy + blended orange, papaya, prunes, and cream, constipation declined p<0.0022; bundled -> attribution_fit=unusable), Abe & Ohtani 2013 (PMID:23183086; Batan Island Philippines 100% Fidelity Level for Carica papaya in constipation), and Parkinson's UK forum discussions (2019 Topic 20523; 2024 Topic 38908) mentioning papaya alongside fiber/fluids. Yeast-fermented papaya nutraceuticals (FPP/Immun'Age) and papaya leaf extracts are strictly excluded as distinct matrices. Safety caveat: latex-fruit allergy cross-reactivity (PMID:37569122) and unripe-papaya latex pregnancy caution.

Full-text OA inspection of the sole preclinical mood/anxiety study—Es-Safi et al. (2021, Molecules, PMC8037343), which administered an organic ethyl-acetate polyphenol fraction of dried Moroccan P. sativum aerial parts (50 & 100 mg/kg/d x 21 d) to normal unstressed Swiss albino mice (n=5/group) in FST, OFT, and light-dark box—revealed four fatal methodological and transferability defects preventing a minimal_signal rating: (1) ZERO statistical test description or p-values appear anywhere in the paper; (2) no randomization or blinding is described with tiny n=5/group in unstressed healthy mice; (3) the extract markedly increased total open-field locomotor tiles crossed (173 vs 147.4 vehicle), creating a classic hyperlocomotor false-positive confound in FST; and (4) the ethyl-acetate fraction's HPLC profile omitted apiin/apigenin, the signature flavone glycoside of culinary parsley leaf. Botanical, matrix & safety caveats: strictly separated culinary Petroselinum crispum (syn. P. sativum) leaf from parsley SEED/essential oil/root (Kreydiyyeh 2002, Essa 2024, Ghitea 2024) and isolated apigenin supplements (Charrière 2024 PMC11084463). Safety notes: high leaf vitamin K1 requires consistent intake in warfarin users (PMID:10902065), whereas 5 g/d dried parsley (84 mg apigenin) for 7 d in 18 healthy humans showed NO antiplatelet or hemostatic effect (Janssen 1998, PMID:9459373); excessive parsley juice caused supratherapeutic sirolimus via CYP3A4/P-gp inhibition in a transplant case (Kurtaran 2021, PMC8058787); apiol-rich seed/oil fractions carry pregnancy cautions (Alobaidi 2024, PMC11672790); and wild poison hemlock (Conium maculatum) poses fatal foraging lookalike toxicity (Şahin 2026, PMID:41643253).

Botanical & safety caveats: strictly separated culinary Pastinaca sativa root from carrot (Daucus carota; noting Persian Zardak/Jazar nomenclature overlap in Kenari 2021 PMC8010426), celery/celeriac (Apium graveolens), cow parsnip (Heracleum), and smaller water-parsnip (Berula erecta, PMC11567558—excluded distinct genus). Raw and cooked parsnip roots retain ~40 ppm linear furanocoumarins/psoralens (xanthotoxin/8-MOP, bergapten/5-MOP, psoralen) that survive boiling/microwaving (Ivie 1981, PMID:7256284), though peeling reduces peel-concentrated levels and a 200 g dietary parsnip meal did NOT lower human UVA1 erythema threshold (Beattie 2007, PMID:17097373). By contrast, topical contact with wild parsnip sap/foliage or parsnip mash plus sunlight causes blistering phytophotodermatitis (PMID:10572825, PMID:32383195, PMC11355232). Apiaceous psoralens also potently inhibit human CYP1A2 (Peterson 2006, PMID:16762476)—a theoretical interaction caveat for CYP1A2-metabolized PD drugs (ropinirole, rasagiline).

Remains Unknown (Researched): Consistent with Round 1 calibration (0/18 directional peanut oil claims), zero controlled human or transferable Parkinson animal trials isolate cold-pressed peanut oil on apathy severity. In the ARISTOTLE RCT (Parilli-Moser 2021, PMID:34656952, Table 3), the polyphenol- and fiber-free peanut-oil control butter (CB, n=19) served strictly as the inactive reference arm without an oil-free control, and showed no significant within-arm improvement on TMT-A (p=0.315), TMT-B (p=0.068), cognitive flexibility (p=0.129), Digit Span (p=0.597), LNS (p=0.702), fluency (p>=0.651), or matrix reasoning (p=0.100); apathy was not assessed.
